pr_body:
LinearizabilityChecker is known to throw OOM when processing long history or partition. This change moves runtime limit for big histories or partitions inside the checker and exposes failure to complete the check via checked exceptions.

Closes: #98432

issue_context.title: OOME in tests due to LinearizabilityChecker overload
issue_context.body:
The following invocation seems to stabilise very well, generating overwhelmingly many events for the linearizability checker to check, leading to an OOME:

`./gradlew ':server:test' --tests "org.elasticsearch.cluster.coordination.AtomicRegisterCoordinatorTests.testAppliesNoMasterBlockAllIfConfigured" -Dtests.seed=9BFB03AB5780EC10`

Seen on a recent commit to `main`, 1fef466f50d9936b6cfe8295e943f1a6c3f6f2f2.

review_comments: Maybe we should do just what we did in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/101357/files#diff-c1fe1b667c241e62ccc27b117ca2daf92b358596f8756e2e9c7a8eec2a8ba4e9L446-L448 and return true in that case? that will avoid having to introduce the new exception and catching it in the calling site.

I think there is a value on distinguishing between `is linearizable` and `could not perform the check`. I am imagining some change could break something and will silently result in `could not perform the check` for all runs. Exception might not be the most elegant solution, we might use enum instead.
Makes sense and since this is a checked exception, callers should handle it anyway 👍
